title: Uncle Julio's: Scale the Queso
briefing: Catering order just dropped: 70 guests. Your standard queso batch serves 20. Scale it. No calculator. Get the math wrong and you waste $40 in cheese or run short mid-event.

expertRecipe.name: Uncle Julio's Queso Blanco (Scaled)
expertRecipe.platingStandard: Smooth, pourable queso. No lumps, no separation. Correct yield for 70 covers. Hold at 135°F+ at all times.

steps.whyExplanation: Every ingredient scales off this number. Wrong multiplier = every measurement is wrong. A 3x batch shorts 10 people. A 4x batch wastes $15+ in cheese.

steps.instruction: Scale white American cheese: 5 lb × 3.5 = 17.5 lb.
steps.whyExplanation: Cheese is the bulk and the cost. Under-scaling means the queso runs out during the event. Over-scaling wastes product that cannot be re-served once held.

steps.instruction: Scale whole milk: 1 qt × 3.5 = 3.5 qt (7 cups).
steps.whyExplanation: Milk controls consistency. Too little and the queso is thick paste. Too much and it's soup. At 3.5x the tolerance for error gets tighter.

steps.instruction: Scale roasted diced jalapeño: 8 oz × 3.5 = 28 oz (1.75 lb).
steps.whyExplanation: Jalapeño heat varies by batch. At 3.5x, taste-test before adding all of it — you can always add more heat, you can't take it out.

steps.instruction: Scale roasted diced tomato: 6 oz × 3.5 = 21 oz.
steps.whyExplanation: Tomato adds moisture and acidity. Too much dilutes the cheese flavor. Measure, don't eyeball — at this batch size, a couple extra ounces changes the texture.
Spices don't always scale linearly at large batches. 3.5 tbsp is correct here, but taste and adjust — cumin can overpower at volume.

steps.instruction: Melt cheese in milk over medium heat, stirring constantly. Add jalapeño, tomato, cumin when smooth.
steps.whyExplanation: High heat scorches cheese to the bottom of the pot. Scorched queso tastes bitter and the batch is ruined — $40 gone. Medium heat and constant stirring prevents it.

steps.instruction: Transfer to hot hold. Maintain 135°F or above. Stir every 15 minutes.
steps.whyExplanation: Queso is a TCS food. Below 135°F it enters the danger zone. After 4 hours below 135°F, the entire batch — 17.5 lb of cheese — must be discarded.

criticalControlPoints.consequence: Scorched queso = bitter taste = entire $40+ batch wasted. Cannot be fixed once burned.
17.5 lb of queso in the danger zone. If held below 135°F for 4 hours, discard the entire batch. $40+ in product lost.
